analysis:
The only changed file is scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py, a CI test harness that exercises the Darkbloom route step in the GitHub workflows. It is not provider runtime code. The PR replaces VALID_SIZES (4x16, 4x24, 8x16, 12x32) with PRODUCTION_SIZES (8x16, 12x32), and moves the PLAN_LANES sizes onto those two values (head lines 76 and 108-121). The line 941 change at base (945 at head) is outside the supplied head excerpt, so I could not inspect it directly. It most likely renames the VALID_SIZES reference in test_ci_sizes_every_routed_macos_job_and_asks_for_the_test_lanes_first to PRODUCTION_SIZES. The head excerpt covers lines 1-565 and the base excerpt covers 565-1060, so the final head test section was not seen.

None of the changes touch provider/coordinator trust boundaries, attestation, encryption, the prefix cache or key handling. The test code stays defensive. It runs against a loopback HTTPS plane with a throwaway certificate, keeps certificate verification on, refuses plain http, and sends nothing for fork PRs. It also checks that the router accepts only the exact profile label arrays, strips workflow-command injection from plane text, and keeps release and credentialed workflows on literal runners (UNROUTED).

No threat-model regression is evident. This is a test-only change that narrows the sizes CI will request to the ones the production plane signs. Whether provider-plan.yml was changed consistently with these tests is outside the supplied evidence and needs the integration pass. If provider-plan.yml and this test drift apart, the likely outcome is a failing test rather than a security weakening. The related T-041 and the other canonical threat IDs are not affected.
